purpose: Behavioral prompts, not a claim all scenarios have executed. Use isolated outputs and report actual visual/playback evidence.

scenarios.request: Make a mint-green round-headed courier robot with amber chest light, short legs and dark-blue boots. Front reference only, size unspecified.
checks: default native 256x256
actual supported image generation or explicit blocker
no animation scope creep
identity and palette/edge visual review

scenarios.request: Use the supplied painting to create front, three-quarter, side and back pixel references.
checks: inspect actual input
no resize-only completion
consistent identity and intentional pixel clusters
inferred-view labels

scenarios.request: Continue these accepted 128x128 views and add a dodge cast.
checks: keep the 128 grid; the canvas may widen for the action
research observed movement
adapt proportions
no unrequested redesign

scenarios.request: Animate a heavy overhead strike for this short-armed character.
checks: contact/reach adapted
nonuniform rhythm
actual new poses
no fixed frame cap

scenarios.request: Repair a detached sleeve around 840 ms without changing timing or design.
checks: direct repair entry
source localized
timing frozen
no lost thin bridge

scenarios.request: Make front, three-quarter, side and back references for this small pixel sprite of a character with repeated parts (e.g. several tails) and a one-sided accessory.
checks: grid kept, or a requested grid change redrawn and recorded
per-view counts and sides match the identity sheet or are explained by occlusion
independent review before delivering the views
inferred-view labels

scenarios.request: Animate a spell cast with a projectile for this existing sprite by splitting it into movable parts.
checks: no new enclosed holes or joint tears
effect keeps moving through body holds
every-frame and independent review
1x playback by the user or a reviewer who can watch, otherwise pending

scenarios.request: Build this pixel character, drawn in a foreshortened mid-air pose, and animate it throwing the dagger it holds.
checks: original pose kept as identity master; neutral base and unseen views labeled inferred
camera view confirmed at the accent poses, face and held props readable
projectile separates at release on its own layer
every fix confirmed on the composited export
independent review rounds told what changed
side-view face and hair rebuilt for the profile, not transplanted from the front
no doubled same-material contours where cut-out parts touch

scenarios.request: Continue this accepted character with a dual-weapon charge, dash and cross slash leaving sword-qi, in an exaggerated game-skill style.
checks: researched poses and prop placements verified at the accent poses: both weapons readable, no bare blade misread as another object
smears and slash marks drawn from each weapon tip's sampled world-space path; a check on rendered pixels shows their ends at the tips
effects layered by depth; the delivered composite equals the stacked exported layers
in-place frames with a root table and/or a wide canvas, effects' coordinate space recorded
effects read on light and dark backgrounds
each effect starts at its causing event's frame and place
hair and clothing trail, lift, overshoot and settle with the body's momentum, without added parts

scenarios.request: Continue this accepted character: throw a weapon, blink to it and catch it, then slam down, with exaggerated game-skill effects.
checks: the weapon leaves along the hand's motion at release; the swing smear's end, the hand's motion and the flight agree
per frame, weapons held plus in flight match the identity sheet; the flying weapon has its own layer
the stab or landing contact shows in rendered pixels and reads as the intended kind; rig shortfalls are reported
each effect's cause is recorded and measured on the rendered frames; no effect has zero visible pixels
identity-color counts are reviewed per frame and recounted after every fix
hair variants still read as hair and change without A/B/A flicker

scenarios.request: Continue this accepted character: a sprint-start charge, two afterimages split off, then the character and each afterimage in turn dash through one point; the character recovers and the afterimages vanish. Flashy game-skill style.
checks: afterimages read as the character with props in the same hands; their markers stay out of the body's identity counts
blocking includes the afterimages as placeholders and an overlay of every moving silhouette; a fresh reviewer sees the blocked key poses before effects
each figure the brief sends through the point visibly passes through it on rendered pixels
contacts and grips are declared and measured in every frame, transitions included; each prop reads as held by the right hand
no back-layer effect shows only as slivers through body gaps; no front effect covers the face or a holding hand where they should read
the GIF loops; its last-to-first step is reviewed as motion, or declared a cut and noted in the final index

scenarios.request: Turn this accepted 256x256 character into a 48x48 game sprite and export it at 4x for a store page.
checks: grid 48 and export scale 4 recorded
redrawn rather than resampled; small identity features kept or dropped on purpose
4x copies made from the 48 grid after review: Scale2x twice by default, nearest neighbor if a direct export was asked
identity facts reviewed at 1x
